display.title: Zman Simchaseinu: Why Sukkos Is a Joy for Us and for Hashem
display.summary_short: Sukkos is called 'the time of our joy', in the plural: a joy for the Jewish people and for Hashem, because after Yom Kippur nothing blocks His blessings from reaching us.
display.summary_long: A Sukkos talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on Chol HaMoed. Uncle Yossi explains that 'zman simchaseinu' is plural: Sukkos is a joy for us and for Hashem too. Hashem always blesses His people, but sins get in the way of the blessings; through teshuvah on Yom Kippur our record was wiped clean, so now His blessings reach us in full. We fill the days with special mitzvos, the sukkah that surrounds us and the four kinds, and we share them with friends and relatives as a true act of Ahavas Yisroel. The joy grows until Simchas Torah, when we dance with the Torah to show our resolutions to learn more and do more mitzvos. 'V'samachta b'chagecha' teaches that this is our own holiday, happening now, in a year the Rebbe said would be filled with miracles.
display.lesson: Sukkos joy comes from a clean slate after Yom Kippur; fill the days with mitzvos and share the joy with others.

date.note: Clip of episode 399, broadcast on Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5750 ('this new year, Tav-Shin-Nun').

sources_cited.note: 'V'samachta b'chagecha', 'as the Torah itself tells us'.
The Rebbe said the year would bring miracles upon miracles.
